AWARD 1.

Vide this order I shall dispose off the 'Detailed Accident Report' (hereinafter referred to as 'DAR')
filed by the police with regard to accident occurred on 04.06.2018 in which injured Ashish Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered grievous injuries.
The DAR was treated as claim petition under Section Ashish Kumar Vs. Haqimuddin & Ors.

Investigating Officer produced petitioner, as well as Suresh Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1') and Jasmeet Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2') of vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration no. RJ09GB 8218 (hereinafter referred to as 'vehicle in question'), which was duly insured with The New India Insurance Company Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 3') Copy of DAR was supplied to all the parties.
Petitioner has also filed separate claim petition, which was tagged with the DAR vide order dated 09.04.2019.

2. Brief facts of the case as per petitioner are that on 04.06.2018 at about 01:30 P.M. in the noon, he alongwith his father travelling on motorcycle and going towards Jahangirpuri from Azadpur and when they reached at Mahendra Park Red Light, the light was just got green, the offending truck bearing No. RJ09GB 8218, driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following/obeying came and hit their motor cycle from the conductor side and he along with his motorcycle fell down on road and sustained injuries.
He was taken to BJRM Hospital for treatment by a PCR van.
3. Respondents no. 1 & 2 have not filed any reply / written statement despite giving repeated opportunities.
They were proceeded ex-parte and their defence was struck off vide order dated 06.06.2022.

Petitioner / PW1 reiterated the averments made in his claim petition that 04.06.2018 at about 01:30 P.M. in the noon, he alongwith his father travelling on motorcycle and going towards Jahangirpuri from Azadpur and when they reached at Mahendra Park Red Light, the light was just got green, the offending truck bearing No. RJ09GB 8218, driven by its driver at a very high speed in a rash and negligent manner without following/obeying came and hit their motor cycle from the conductor side and he along with his motorcycle fell down on road and sustained injuries.

Further, PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondents no. 1 and 2 particularly by respondent no. 1 nor any witness has been examined by them to prove that respondent no. 1 was not rash and negligent or that accident had occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner or that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that it is false case against him.
Moreover, no written statement has been filed by them.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his MLC filed MACT no. 43/19 by SUNIL Ashish Kumar Vs. Haqimuddin & Ors.

Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning &
Pressing Co. (P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC 745 Civil Appeal No. 2071 of 1968, decided on March 25, 1977 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, wherein it was held as under: - "The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident "speaks for itself" or tell's its own story.

entities.text:
Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning &
Pressing Co. (P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC 745 Civil Appeal No. 2071 of 1968
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are cases in which the accident speaks for itself so that it is sufficient for the plaintiff to prove the accident and nothing more.
It will then be for the defendant to establish that the accident happened due to some other cause than his own negligence.

Salmond on the Law of Torts (15th Ed.) at p. 306 states: "The maxim res ipsa loquitur applies whenever it is so improbable that such an accident would have happened without the negligence of the defendant that a reasonable jury could find without further evidence that it was so caused."

In Halsbury's Laws of England, 3rd Ed., Vol. 28, at p. 77, the position is stated thus:
"An exception to the general rule that the burden of proof of the alleged negligence is in the first instance on the plaintiff occurs wherever the facts already established are Ashish Kumar vs Hakmuddin on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188494013/
5 such that .the proper and natural inference arising from them is ,that the injury complained of was caused by the defendant's negligence, or where the event charged as negligence "tells its own story' of negligence on the part of the defendant, the story so told being clear and unambiguous."
Further

, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh,
Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under:-
"The plaintiff can prove the accident but cannot prove how it happened to establish negligence.

entities.text: Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs. Phulwant Mahendra Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.
The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of MACT no. 43/19 by SUNIL Ashish Kumar Vs.

9.

As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Accordingly, the question of right of the injured for claiming of compensation is decided in favour of the petitioner.

Now, the second part of the issue in hand with respect to the quantum of compensation is to be adjudicated and below are the finding: -
10.
Petitioner as PW1 deposed that after the accident he was taken to BJRM Hospital for treatment.

He further deposed that he was aged about 26 years at the time of accident and working privately and earning Rs. 20,000/- per month and due to this accident he could not continue his work for two months.
He relied upon the treatment record and medical bills collectively Ex. PW1/2 and PW1/3.
He also relied upon this ITRs collectively Ex. PW1/4 and claimed a compensation of Rs. 5 lakhs on various heads.

The total original medical bills placed and proved on record are amounting to Rs.
1,50,197/-.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs. 1,50,197/- is allowed to the petitioner towards medical expenditure.

Through, there is no evidence except deposition of petitioner to verify that he spent any Ashish Kumar vs Hakmuddin on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188494013/

However, seeing nature of injuries suffered by petitioner, a sum of Rs. 15,000/- towards special diet and Rs. 15,000/-

sentences.text: 11. As far as loss of income during the treatment is concerned, through petitioner as PW1 has deposed that at the time of accident he was earning Rs. 20,000/- per month but in his cross examination PW1 / petitioner admitted that he has no document to show that he was earning such amount.

Though, the income of petitioner could not be proved nor any educational qualification document has been filed but considering the age of petitioner, it is presumed that he would have been earning at least Rs. 15,000/- per month.

Accordingly, Rs.45,000/- (15,000x3) is allowed to the petitioner for loss of income during the period of treatment and during this period he must have taken the services of an attendant and hence a sum of Rs.15,000/- (5000x3) towards attendant charges are awarded to the petitioner.
12. Further, apart from the above mentioned amounts, petitioner is entitled for compensation regarding mental pain and suffering, disfiguration etc.

Accordingly, after giving due weight-age to the totality of the facts and circumstances of the case, a sum of Rs.50,000/- for mental pain and physical shock as well as for pain and suffering due to this accident, Rs. 50,000/- towards loss of amenities of life and Rs.50,000/- for loss of inconvenience, hardship disappointment, frustration,
mention stress dejectment and unhappiness in future life etc. are also awarded to the petitioner,
making a total sum of Rs. 3,90,197/-, details of which is mentioned in the attached proforma.
In the light of the above discussion, the aspect of liability of the respondents is to be adjudicated and findings are mentioned below: -
13 . Admittedly, the vehicle was insured.
However, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. has taken certain technical pleas.
The main contention of the respondent no. 3 is MACT no. 43/19 SUNIL KUMAR Ashish Kumar Vs. Haqimuddin & Ors.

Postal receipt is exhibited as and Ex-R3W1/2.

R3W1 further relied upon the DL verification report of D/L No. 227010/UKL in the name of Hakimuddin issued by the District Transport Office Ukhrul district, Manipur EX-R3W1/4 in which the D/L is fake and not issued from there office.
She further deposed that I.O has also filed the charge sheet U/S 468/471 of IPC Act.

R3W1 has not at all been cross examined on behalf of respondents no. 1 and 2 nor any valid driving licence of respondent no. 1 has been produced and all inter alia shows that respondent no. 1 was having no valid driving licence at the Ashish Kumar vs Hakmuddin on 7 August, 2025

But it is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.3 on the date of accident.

Hence, being insurer, respondent no. 3 / Ins. opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Though,
accident has not been disputed but by the Ins. Co., however PW1 / petitioner has been cross examined by the respondent no. 3 but nothing material has come on record to disbelieve the testimony of PW1/petitioner, as being injured petitioner is natural eye-witness of accident.
Further, PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondents no. 1 and 2 particularly by respondent no. 1 nor any witness has been examined by them to prove that respondent no. 1 was not rash and negligent or that accident had occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner or that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that it is false case against him.
Moreover, no written statement has been filed by them.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his MLC filed MACT no. 43/19 by SUNIL Ashish Kumar Vs. Haqimuddin & Ors.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Relying upon judgment in Pushpabai Purshottam Udeshi & Ors vs Ranjit Ginning &
Pressing Co. (P) Ltd. & Anr. 1977 (2) SCC 745 Civil Appeal No. 2071 of 1968, decided on March 25, 1977 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, wherein it was held as under: - "The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident "speaks for itself" or tell's its own story.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of MACT no. 43/19 by SUNIL Ashish Kumar Vs.
Haqimuddin & Ors.
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
12. Further, apart from the above mentioned amounts, petitioner is entitled for compensation regarding mental pain and suffering, disfiguration etc.
The main contention of the respondent no. 3 is MACT no. 43/19 SUNIL KUMAR Ashish Kumar Vs. Haqimuddin & Ors.
But it is not in dispute that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent no.3 on the date of accident.
Hence, being insurer, respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. is primarily liable to pay compensation to the petitioner, but since it has been able to prove breach of terms and conditions of insurance policy Ex.R3W1/3, it has given liberty to recover the compensation amount from the respondents no. 1 and 2 jointly and severally but after paying the compensation to the petitioner.
